interpretation_limits: A PASS is development evidence only; sealed holdout validation remains mandatory before profile creation or promotion.
Every detector candidate has exactly two spheres: one heel and one forefoot.
The nine unique detector spheres in each offline batch are shared placement samples for ten independent two-sensor pairs, not a nine-sensor runtime detector.
The mesh is used only offline to place the two simple spheres and enforce proximity and bottom-offset limits.
Thresholds 0.5/0.25 N, dwell 30 ms, FSM, timing gates, primary load evidence, and event-guard routing are unchanged from V7.
Toe-latch recontact remains a separate diagnostic; the detector gate requires at least 30 ms causal clear before the next accepted HS onset.
The runtime RL load-routing gap remains unresolved, so a development winner is not promotable or deployable.
No policy, training, rollout, runtime default, FSM, active profile, or sealed data is modified or evaluated.
objective: Keep the forefoot near the V5 location that preserves causal rearming, and test whether small combined heel anterior/depth changes can delay HS by about 2.5 ms while eliminating the 6 ms initial heel-to-forefoot gap. Every candidate remains one heel sphere plus one forefoot sphere and must pass at both 10 ms and 1 ms.
